newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank seen selling dollars - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank seen selling dollars - dealers.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was seen selling dollars at 1,700-1,710 levs at 1300 local time (1000 GMT) on Monday to stabilise the national currency which was headed for a steep fall in the morning, dealers said.
"The central bank is selling dollars at 1,700-1,710 and the lev has stabilised around these levels," a commercial bank dealer told Reuters.
Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov told reporters on Monday that the BNB now was strong enough to support the lev near its current levels.
BNB foreign exchange reserves rose to $1.146 billion in April from $554 million a month earlier due to net dollar purchases.

The lev weakened to 1,750-1,950 per dollar in opening quotes on a nervous interbank market on Monday as dollar shortcovering was carried over from Friday due to a cut in the central bank main interest rate.

It settled between 1,650-1,740 in late morning because foreign currency demand for shortcovering was lower than expected and big final dollar buyers like energy and fuel importers were not seen bidding for foreign currency.
The lev closed at 1,685-1,700 per dollar on Friday.
The new main interest rate of 4.29 percent monthly, down from previous 5.20 percent, became effective on Monday. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
